The khaen is the national instrument of Laos, Hornbostel–Sachs 412.132. Its bamboo pipes are set into a small hollowed hardwood wind chest, and blowing sets free reeds of brass or silver sounding; with the Chinese sheng it belongs to the free-reed family. A player can use it for solos, in ensembles, or to accompany the mor lam singers of Laos and Isan, and it is often paired with the plucked instrument the phin. It is found among the Thai, Lao and Mon communities of Laos, Thailand, Vietnam and Cambodia, and it is used on occasions such as the Cambodian dance-drama “lakhon ken”.

A beginner can start with a small twelve-pipe model, practising steady breath and basic sound production. The instrument can be played solo, in an ensemble or as accompaniment, and it is often paired with plucked instruments. Each instrument cannot be retuned once the reeds are fixed and the pipes cut, so a beginner should practise at the pitch the instrument already has instead of trying to change it.

笙（寮國）可見於寮國生活、柬埔寨舞劇「拉坤肯」主奏，以及寮國與伊善的摩蘭獨唱伴奏: The khaen appears in Lao daily life, as the lead instrument in the Cambodian dance-drama “lakhon ken”, and as accompaniment to mor lam solo singing in Laos and Isan; it can also play solo, in ensembles, or with the traditional fretted plucked lute. It is used as well by the Thai and Muong peoples of Vietnam and by Lao communities in Stung Treng province in Cambodia. Lockwood, Adler, Loeb and Ivanova have written scores for it.
笙（寮國）為寮國國家樂器，屬自由簧氣鳴樂器，與中國笙有關聯；西方自由簧樂器自十八: The khaen is the national instrument of Laos, a free-reed aerophone related to the Chinese sheng; Western free-reed instruments developed from the Chinese sheng from the eighteenth century onward, and specimens of the related sheng reached St Petersburg in Russia. Its music helps bind family and society together in Lao social life, and in 2017 it was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The instrument is also found in Isan in Thailand, among the Thai and Muong peoples of Vietnam, and in the Cambodian dance-drama “lakhon ken”.
